subject: Human Evolution
title: Zoonotic Diseases
description: A short lesson to help you apply Zoonotic Diseases.

hook.text: COVID, Ebola, HIV—all jumped from animals to humans. Why do we keep catching animal diseases?

buildup.text: As humans expanded into new habitats, they contacted new species and their viruses.

discovery.text: Domesticating animals 10,000 years ago created permanent close contact—a pathogen highway.

twist.text: Dense farming villages gave diseases stable host populations. Nomads had too few people to sustain epidemics.

climax.text: Most deadly pandemics in history trace back to the moment humans started living with their livestock.

quiz.question: Why did zoonotic diseases increase with farming?
options: Close contact with livestock created pathogen transmission routes
